[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This document is the step-by-step bootstrap guide for standing up the Golden Path Platform from scratch — before any Golden Path is authored and before any product team can adopt a path. It covers three sequential bodies of work: governance setup, Golden Path Platform infrastructure setup, and the repeatable per-path authoring sequence. None of these can be skipped or reordered.

This document describes what Platform Engineering and Platform Infrastructure must build. What product teams do once the platform is operational is documented in [GUID-GOV-PROC-003](./GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md). What Platform Engineering does to author each individual Golden Path bundle is documented in [GUID-GOV-PROC-004](./GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md).
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- Provides a clear, sequenced setup guide that does not currently exist in the repo — preventing Platform Engineering teams from starting in the wrong order or missing prerequisites
- Separates one-time platform setup work from per-path authoring work, enabling accurate planning and resource allocation
- Defines the minimum viable platform state required before the first product team can be onboarded to any path

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The Golden Path system has three distinct layers: governance decisions, a platform that manages and enforces paths, and content (the individual paths) within that platform. An organization cannot author or publish a Golden Path until the platform exists. The platform cannot operate without the governance decisions being made first. This document sequences all three layers so that setup proceeds without blocking dependencies.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The Golden Path Platform consists of four components that must exist before any path can be published:

| Component | What it is | Who builds it |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog Git repo | Repository storing all Golden Path files | Platform Engineering |
| Pipeline Templates repo | Repository storing the `conformance-check` script and shared pipeline templates | Platform Engineering |
| `conformance-check` script | Shared script that validates product team repos against a declared Golden Path | Platform Engineering |
| Compliance Evidence Store | Storage endpoint receiving pass/fail results from every pipeline run | Platform Infrastructure |

Each Golden Path is content stored inside the Catalog repo. The `conformance-check` script enforces each path's rules. The Evidence Store retains the enforcement record for audit purposes. None of these components are provided by a commercial product — they are built by Platform Engineering using standard Git, scripting, and storage infrastructure.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

No single document in the repo describes the end-to-end setup sequence from a blank-slate organization to a published, enforced Golden Path. Individual pattern and guidance documents describe their own prerequisites, but a new Platform Engineering team must synthesize those prerequisites across many documents to understand what to build first. This guidance consolidates that sequencing into a single actionable playbook.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#success-criteria]

### Success Criteria

| Success Area | Metrics | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation complete | All one-time setup steps verified | All checklist items passing before first path authoring begins |
| First path published | First Golden Path reaches `active` status in the catalog | Within the planned delivery window |
| First team onboarded | First product team pipeline runs conformance gate in warn-only mode | Within a defined window following first path publication |
| Enforcement active | Gate promoted to fail-hard mode | False positive rate below 1% |

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#principle-1-governance-decisions-before-tooling]

#### Principle 1: Governance Decisions Before Tooling

**Description:** ARB process and exception management procedures must be defined before any tooling is built or tested. Running a conformance gate without an exception process leaves teams blocked with no recourse.

**Rationale:** The conformance gate fails builds. If there is no published process for how a team requests an exception or gets a triage response, teams will find workarounds — defeating the purpose of the gate. The exception process is a prerequisite, not an afterthought.

**Application:** Complete both governance steps (ARB update and exception process definition) before writing a single line of tooling code.
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#principle-2-platform-infrastructure-before-path-content]

#### Principle 2: Platform Infrastructure Before Path Content

**Description:** The Catalog repo, Pipeline Templates repo, `conformance-check` script, and Evidence Store must all exist before any Golden Path bundle components are authored.

**Rationale:** Path content references tooling (check IDs, evidence store endpoints, pipeline template structures). Authoring content before the tooling is stable means rework when the tooling changes.

**Application:** Treat the four platform infrastructure components as a single deliverable that must be complete before Phase 3 (per-path authoring) begins.
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#principle-3-the-runtime-platform-is-a-dependency-not-a-deliverable]

#### Principle 3: The Runtime Platform Is a Dependency, Not a Deliverable

**Description:** The Golden Path Platform does not build the runtime environment where workloads run. That environment (whatever compute, secrets, and artifact registry the org uses) must already exist or be provisioned in parallel by Platform Infrastructure.

**Rationale:** The Golden Path Infrastructure Module provisions workload-level resources *within* a runtime platform — it does not provision the platform itself. Authoring the Infrastructure Module requires a real target environment to write and test against.

**Application:** Confirm that the target runtime platform and associated services (secrets store, artifact registry) are provisioned and accessible before beginning Infrastructure Module authoring in Phase 3.
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#principle-4-the-per-path-sequence-is-fixed]

#### Principle 4: The Per-Path Sequence Is Fixed

**Description:** Within each Golden Path authoring effort, the Verification Contract must be authored first because every other bundle component depends on the check IDs it defines.

**Rationale:** The Application Scaffold must produce a structure that passes Layer 1 checks. The `conformance-check` script must implement those same checks. The CI/CD Pipeline Template wires those check IDs at specific stages. None of these can be finalized without stable check IDs from the Verification Contract.

**Application:** Do not begin Scaffold, Infrastructure Module, Security Template, or Pipeline Template authoring until the Verification Contract Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs are stable.

---
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#overview]

### Overview

The work is organized into three sequential phases. Phases 1 and 2 are one-time setup. Phase 3 repeats for every Golden Path added to the catalog.

```
Phase 1: Governance Setup          (one-time)
    └── unblocks ──► Phase 2: Platform Infrastructure   (one-time)
                         └── unblocks ──► Phase 3: Per Golden Path Authoring  (repeats)
```

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-1--update-the-arb-process]

#### Step 1 — Update the ARB Process

Add Golden Path review as a standing agenda item with a defined review cycle. Confirm the ARB has the authority to approve, reject, or require changes to path proposals and bundle submissions.

**Deliverable:** ARB charter or process document updated; review cycle confirmed.

---
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-2--define-and-publish-the-exception-management-process]

#### Step 2 — Define and Publish the Exception Management Process

Write and publish the process that governs what happens when the conformance gate blocks a product team's build. At minimum this must specify:

- How a team raises an exception request
- Who triages it and what the response SLA is
- What constitutes an approved exception vs. a required remediation
- How exception records are tracked and closed

**Deliverable:** Exception management process published at [GUID-GOV-PROC-002](./GUID-GOV-PROC-002-exception-management-process.md) and accessible to all engineering teams.

> **Critical:** The conformance gate must NOT be set to fail-hard mode on any team's pipeline until this process is published and the triage SLA is in place. Fail-hard enforcement without a published exception process leaves teams blocked with no recourse.

---

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#phase-2-golden-path-platform-infrastructure]

### Phase 2: Golden Path Platform Infrastructure

*One-time. These four components form the platform that all Golden Paths run on. Must be complete before Phase 3 begins.*

page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-3--create-the-catalog-git-repo]

#### Step 3 — Create the Catalog Git Repo

Create the repository that will store all Golden Path files. This is the authoritative source for every path's Verification Contract, Application Scaffold, Infrastructure Module, Security Template, and CI/CD Pipeline Template.

**Repo:** `{org}/gp-catalog` (or equivalent naming per your Git hosting platform)

**Initial structure to create:**
```
catalog/
    verification-contracts/
    templates/
    infrastructure/
    security/
    ci-cd/
    compliance/
catalog-index.yaml          ← machine-readable index of all published paths
```

**Access:** Platform Engineering has write access to `catalog/` branches. Product teams have read access only.

**Deliverable:** Repo created; initial directory structure in place; access controls configured.

---
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-4--create-the-pipeline-templates-repo]

#### Step 4 — Create the Pipeline Templates Repo

Create the repository that will store the `conformance-check` script and shared pipeline templates consumed by product team pipelines. This is a separate repo from the Catalog so that pipeline tooling can be versioned and released independently of path content.

**Repo:** `{org}/platform-pipeline-templates` (ADO) or equivalent

**Initial structure to create:**
```
steps/
    conformance-gate.yml        ← pipeline template step (ADO) or action.yml (GitHub)
scripts/
    conformance_check.py        ← the conformance-check script (stub; built in Step 5)
README.md
```

**Access:** Platform Engineering has write access. Product teams have read access only. Releases are controlled via version tags.

**Deliverable:** Repo created; initial directory structure in place; access controls configured.

---
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-5--build-the-conformance-check-script]

#### Step 5 — Build the `conformance-check` Script

Build the script that checks product team workload repositories against a declared Golden Path's Verification Contract. This script is the implementation of Layer 1 (Conformance Gate) from PTN-INFRA-GOV-001.

**What the script must do:**

1. **Catalog Loader** — read the `service.yaml` (or equivalent) at the repo root to identify the declared Golden Path ID, then fetch that path's Verification Contract YAML from the Catalog repo
2. **Rule Evaluator** — loop through every Layer 1 check in the Verification Contract and execute it. Layer 1 checks are file system operations only (no running service required): file existence, directory structure, metadata field presence, dependency manifest scanning
3. **Evidence Writer** — write a `conformance-report.json` with the pass/fail result per check ID and upload it as a pipeline artifact
4. **Exception Router** — on any check failure, call the issue tracker API to create a triage ticket and post a notification to the designated alerting channel

**Implementation note:** This script is a custom build — no off-the-shelf tool provides this functionality. It can be implemented as a Python script, Go binary, or shell script.

**Important:** At this stage, the script is built as a runner. The specific Layer 1 check IDs it executes for each path come from the Verification Contract authored in Phase 3. The script reads rules from the contract at runtime — you are building the execution engine here, not hardcoding rules for any specific path.

**Deliverable:** Script checked into the Pipeline Templates repo; pipeline template step (`conformance-gate.yml`) wiring the script into a callable pipeline step; v1 version tag released.

---
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-6--provision-the-compliance-evidence-store]

#### Step 6 — Provision the Compliance Evidence Store

Provision the storage endpoint that receives pass/fail results from every pipeline run. Every build across every product team writes a structured record to this store. It is the audit trail for the entire Golden Path system.

**What it must support:**
- Accept structured JSON records from pipeline agents (the `evidence-uploader` tool calls it at Stage 17 of every build)
- Records are queryable by `path_id`, `commit_sha`, and `build_id`
- Append-only access control (pipeline agents can write; no agent can overwrite or delete)
- Retention period defined and reviewed with Legal and Compliance

**Implementation options:** An indexed blob store, a purpose-built database, or an existing compliance platform that accepts structured artifact uploads. The specific technology depends on your platform's existing capabilities. See PTN-GOV-AI-004 for the evidence schema and record structure.

**Deliverable:** Evidence Store provisioned; write endpoint accessible from CI/CD pipeline agents; read endpoint accessible for compliance reporting; retention policy configured.

---
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#phase-3-per-golden-path-authoring]

### Phase 3: Per Golden Path Authoring

*Repeats for every new path added to the catalog. Steps are sequenced — do not begin a step until its dependency is satisfied.*

page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-7--author-the-verification-contract-no-runtime-platform-required]

#### Step 7 — Author the Verification Contract *(no runtime platform required)*

Define every rule the workload class must follow and assign a stable check ID to each rule. This is a YAML file stored in the Catalog repo.

This step must come first. Every subsequent step in this phase depends on stable check IDs from this contract.

**Reference:** [GUID-GOV-IMPL-001](../implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-001-golden-path-verification-contract-authoring-guidance.md)

**Deliverable:** `catalog/verification-contracts/{path-id}-verification-contract.yaml` with all Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs stable.

---
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-8--author-the-application-scaffold-no-runtime-platform-required]

#### Step 8 — Author the Application Scaffold *(no runtime platform required)*

Create the workload repository template that product teams instantiate to create a new workload on this path. The scaffold must produce output that passes all Layer 1 checks defined in Step 7.

**Reference:** [GUID-APP-IMPL-003](../../application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-003-golden-path-scaffold-authoring-guidance.md)

**Deliverable:** `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` with `template.yaml` and all required stub files.

---
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-9--add-this-paths-layer-1-rules-to-the-conformance-check-script]

#### Step 9 — Add This Path's Layer 1 Rules to the `conformance-check` Script

The script runner was built in Step 5. Now register this path's Layer 1 check IDs so the script knows what to evaluate when a product team repo declares this path. Because the script reads rules from the Verification Contract at runtime, this step may require only confirming the new contract is accessible from the catalog endpoint — not modifying the script itself.

**Deliverable:** Verified that the `conformance-check` script correctly reads and evaluates all Layer 1 checks from the new path's Verification Contract.

---
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-10--author-the-infrastructure-module-requires-runtime-platform]

#### Step 10 — Author the Infrastructure Module *(requires runtime platform)*

Write the IaC that provisions this workload's runtime resources (isolation boundary, workload identity, secrets access) within the target runtime platform. The target platform must already exist and be accessible.

**Reference:** [GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001](../../infrastructure/implementation/GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001-golden-path-infrastructure-module-authoring-guidance.md)

**Deliverable:** `catalog/infrastructure/{path-id}/` with `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`, and `infrastructure-module-manifest.yaml`.

---
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-11--author-the-security-template-requires-step-10-outputs]

#### Step 11 — Author the Security Template *(requires Step 10 outputs)*

Write the network policies, certificate configuration, and OPA policy bundle for this path. Requires the workload identity reference that comes from Step 10.

**Reference:** [GUID-SEC-IMPL-001](../../security/implementation/GUID-SEC-IMPL-001-golden-path-security-template-authoring-guidance.md)

**Deliverable:** `catalog/security/{path-id}/` with all policy files and `security-template-manifest.yaml`.

---
page_texts.41:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-12--author-the-cicd-pipeline-template-requires-steps-7-8-10-and-11-all-stable]

#### Step 12 — Author the CI/CD Pipeline Template *(requires Steps 7, 8, 10, and 11 all stable)*

Author the pipeline template that wires all four verification layers together and produces compliance evidence on every build. Requires stable check IDs from Step 7, confirmed unit test invocation pattern from Step 8, and artifact registry/runtime platform details from Steps 10–11.

**Reference:** [GUID-TECH-IMPL-001](../../technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md)

**Deliverable:** `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/` with the platform-specific pipeline template and `workflow-params.yaml`.

---
page_texts.42:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-13--end-to-end-dry-run]

#### Step 13 — End-to-End Dry Run

Instantiate a test workload repo from the scaffold (Step 8), run the full pipeline with `dry_run: true`, confirm:

- All 17 required stages pass
- The `conformance-check` passes on the scaffold-instantiated repo
- A compliance evidence record is written to the Evidence Store

Then run again with `dry_run: false` to confirm deployment stages also succeed. The ARB submission package must include the run ID of the successful `dry_run: false` execution.

**Deliverable:** Successful pipeline run ID; confirmed Evidence Store entry; dry run report.

---
page_texts.43:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-14--arb-submission-and-approval]

#### Step 14 — ARB Submission and Approval

Submit the complete bundle (all five components + dry run evidence) for ARB review. The ARB evaluates the bundle against the patterns and standards defined in the catalog governance framework.

**Deliverable:** ARB approval record.

---
page_texts.44:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-15--publish-to-catalog]

#### Step 15 — Publish to Catalog

Merge all component files to the Catalog repo main branch. Update `catalog-index.yaml` with the new path entry. Set `status: active`.

**Deliverable:** Path visible in the catalog index; `status: active`.

---
page_texts.45:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-16--onboard-first-team-in-warn-only-mode]

#### Step 16 — Onboard First Team in Warn-Only Mode

Configure the conformance gate in warn-only mode for the first adopting product team. The gate runs and reports issues but does not block builds. Measure the false positive rate — the percentage of gate failures that are bugs in the gate itself rather than genuine conformance violations.

**Target:** False positive rate below 1% before proceeding to Step 17.

**Deliverable:** First team's pipeline running with gate in warn-only mode; false positive tracking in place.

---
page_texts.46:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#step-17--promote-to-fail-hard-mode]

#### Step 17 — Promote to Fail-Hard Mode

Once the false positive rate is below 1% and the exception management process from Step 2 has been confirmed to work end-to-end (at least one exception ticket raised and resolved), promote the gate to fail-hard mode.

**Gate condition:** Exception process published ✅ + false positive rate < 1% ✅

**Deliverable:** Gate running in fail-hard mode; all product teams on this path notified.

---
page_texts.48:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#governance-framework]

### Governance Framework

This guidance is owned by Platform Engineering. The ARB governs the approval of individual Golden Paths submitted through this process. Exception management is governed by GUID-GOV-PROC-002.

Any change to the one-time platform setup steps (Phase 1 and Phase 2) that affects enforcement behavior — for example, changing how the `conformance-check` reports failures, or changing the Evidence Store schema — must be reviewed by the ARB before deployment, as it affects all published paths simultaneously.
page_texts.49:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-005-golden-path-platform-bootstrap-guidance.md#risk-management]

### Risk Management

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Gate promoted to fail-hard before exception process is published | Product teams blocked with no recourse; gate bypass workarounds proliferate | Step 2 is a prerequisite; gate MUST NOT run fail-hard without a published exception process |
| Pipeline Templates repo write access is too broad | Product teams modify the `conformance-check` script, defeating governance | Write access restricted to Platform Engineering; product teams have read-only access |
| Evidence Store write access is too broad | Pipeline agents can overwrite or delete evidence records | Append-only access model; no agent has delete or update permissions |
| Verification Contract check IDs change after downstream components are authored | Scaffold, script, and pipeline template go out of sync with the contract | Treat check IDs as stable once Layer 1 and Layer 2 are declared; version the contract alongside the path |

---
page_texts.51:

### Decision Dependencies

The choice of CI/CD platform (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, or Jenkins) made during Phase 2 determines the template format used in every per-path pipeline template (Step 12) and the syntax of the pipeline template step in the Pipeline Templates repo (Step 4). This decision should be locked before Phase 2 begins and treated as a platform constant.
